prompt:
Pixel art emblem of the zodiac sign TAURUS: a bull's head seen from the front, broad and square, with a wide crescent of horns and a gold ring, centred inside a thin-lined regular hexagon frame (all six sides equal) with a low rounded hill and a few simple flowers behind it.

This is a SYMBOL, not a character: a timeless emblem like a heraldic crest, a carved totem, a stained-glass roundel or a constellation card. Front-facing, perfectly symmetrical, still and dignified. The face is calm and neutral with a steady level gaze, so that anyone born under the sign can see themselves in it. No cartoon expression, no grin, no frown, no eyebrows, no mascot, no cuteness, no story, no pose. Never fierce or scary: no fangs, no snarl. The sign's nature shows only through form: broad, heavy, level shapes, a wide flat brow and a thick neck: calm, patience, steadiness and great strength at rest.

Style: bold simplified geometric shapes, 16-bit console pixel art, hard square pixels, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no gradients, no dithering. Drawn on a 96 x 96 pixel grid, shown enlarged so each pixel is a clear square. The whole image has a flat solid BLACK background, edge to edge.

Palette: exactly four flat colours plus black: cream, chestnut brown, ochre, leaf green. At most two flat shades of each, nothing else.

Composition: the emblem fills about 65% of the frame. Square image, no text, no letters, no watermark, no signature.
